title: Bunny Codes: Broadening Superconducting Quantum Error Correction Capability through Advanced Control Engineering
authors: Runshi Zhou, Xingye Yuan, Linghang Kong, Fang Zhang, Kai Zhang, Zhaohui Yang, Jianxin Chen
abstract: Drawing on advances in superconducting qubit control schemes that unlock enriched native gate sets at the hardware level, we systematically examine how harnessing this enlarged physical two-qubit gate pool -- specifically CNOT and CXSWAP -- streamlines syndrome extraction for certain qLDPC codes with nonlocal stabilizers. Through an exhaustive search, we discover a set of qLDPC codes with various stabilizer weights and distances that can be implemented on the two-dimensional nearest-neighbor qubit connectivity native to superconducting hardware while achieving performance equivalent to that of the direct CNOT implementation requiring long-range interactions. We refer to those codes as Bunny codes. Across all code distances we examine, the best Bunny codes with weight-6 stabilizers in periodic boundary conditions have a code rate approximately $3\times$ that of the toric code; when converted to open boundary conditions, they retain an approximately $2\times$ code rate advantage over the rotated surface code. In circuit-level simulation, we find that some Bunny codes exhibit logical error rates an order of magnitude lower than toric codes with comparable code rates. Our results demonstrate that high-performance quantum error correction can be achieved using an expanded gate set rather than long-range couplers, thereby significantly reducing hardware complexity.
summary: The paper proposes 'Bunny codes' to advance superconducting Quantum Error Correction by leveraging an expanded native two-qubit gate set (CNOT and CXSWAP). Through systematic circuit construction and simulation, they demonstrate that these codes achieve superior code rates and lower logical error rates compared to established codes like the Toric code. This work proves that high performance can be achieved through smarter control engineering rather than requiring complex physical hardware modifications.
main_problem: The primary challenge is achieving high-performance Quantum Error Correction (QEC) on superconducting qubits while overcoming limitations imposed by restricted physical qubit connectivity and the need to avoid complex, long-range couplers.
main_result: The authors introduce 'Bunny codes,' which utilize an expanded native gate set (CNOT and CXSWAP) to achieve significantly higher code rates ($\sim 3	imes$ Toric code rate in periodic boundaries) and lower logical error rates compared to standard surface codes, all while maintaining local connectivity.
method: The approach involves a bottom-up search strategy on 2D lattices, exhaustively constructing syndrome extraction circuits by tracking qubit displacements caused by sequential application of CNOT/CXSWAP gates. These verified circuits are then used to calculate code parameters and simulate logical error rates.
model_or_system: The system is superconducting qubits arranged on a 2D planar grid (e.g., square or hexagonal lattice). The model relies on the assumption that the hardware natively supports an enlarged two-qubit gate set, specifically CNOT and CXSWAP gates.
key_observables: Code rate, logical error rates ($\epsilon$), code distance ($d$), and required qubit connectivity/stabilizer weights.
important_parameters: Stabilizer weights (e.g., weight-6), lattice size ($l 	imes m$), physical error rate ($\epsilon$), and the ratio of achievable code rate to that of the Toric or Surface codes.
main_assumptions: The hardware supports CNOT and CXSWAP gates with equivalent gate duration, allowing for syndrome extraction without long-range couplers. Translational symmetry is assumed during the construction phase.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate lattice setups (surface/hexagonal), basic unit structures showing qubit labeling and couplers, examples of syndrome extraction circuits tracking sub-lattice displacements, and final comparisons of code rates and logical error rates for various codes under periodic and open boundary conditions.
paper_structure: The paper systematically develops a method to map physical gate actions (CNOT/CXSWAP) onto mathematical qubit displacement vectors. It then uses this framework to search for high-rate qLDPC codes, rigorously verifies the syndrome extraction circuits via commutation checks, and finally evaluates performance metrics like code rate and logical error rates on various lattice geometries.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it directly addresses hardware constraints in quantum computing. By showing that gate set expansion can bypass complex physical wiring (long-range couplers), it offers a more scalable path toward fault-tolerant computation, which is crucial for realizing large-scale quantum processors.
